description: Add a read-only `find-duplicates` command family to `rt` that discovers repeated statement blocks across a solution without requiring a seed example. Phase 1 ships deterministic structural duplicate detection (exact + normalized-identifier/literal matching). Phase 2 adds overlap suppression, scope/size filters, and JSON output. Phase 3 adds an optional `--mode semantic` backed by a pluggable IEmbeddingProvider (with a bundled local/deterministic provider). Phase 4 surfaces extraction-readiness diagnostics that a future extract workflow can consume. Automatic rewriting is out of scope for v1 — discovery is strictly separate from mutation.
ralph_instructions: Architectural rule: every Command class is a thin shell — its ExecuteAsync must only load the workspace and delegate to <Name>Core.RunAsync(...). All Roslyn logic lives in src/RoslynTools/Core/<Name>Core.cs. For find-duplicates, the Core layer owns: candidate-window enumeration, normalization, grouping, ranking, and (in US-206) the IEmbeddingProvider abstraction. Do NOT pull semantic-mode dependencies into the default structural path — FR-3 requires structural mode to work fully offline with no extra packages. Reuse SymbolFinder/SemanticModel/SyntaxTree APIs; do not match via regex over raw text (FR-4). Verification (every story, non-negotiable): `dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx`, `dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal`, `dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes`. Do NOT skip the format check. Use /tdd (red→green→refactor). Dogfood `rt` for any C# symbol navigation / refactoring during implementation; log gaps to tasks/dogfood-gaps.md.

userStories.title: find-duplicates — structural exact-clone discovery (skeleton)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to find repeated code blocks across a solution without specifying a sample first so I can identify extraction opportunities quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/RoslynTools/Commands/FindDuplicatesCommand.cs (thin shell) — alias `fd`
Create src/RoslynTools/Core/FindDuplicatesCore.cs with a RunAsync entry point: (Solution sln, FindDuplicatesOptions options) -> IReadOnlyList<DuplicateGroup>
FindDuplicatesCommand.ExecuteAsync is ≤ 20 lines (parse options + delegate + format output)
CLI: `rt find-duplicates --solution <path> [--min-statements N] [--min-occurrences N]` — defaults: min-statements=3, min-occurrences=2

Enumerate candidate statement windows from every MethodDeclarationSyntax / LocalFunctionStatementSyntax body across the solution; each window is a contiguous sequence of StatementSyntax from a BlockSyntax
Group windows by a verbatim-syntax hash (trivia stripped only — NO identifier/literal canonicalisation in this story; that is US-202)

Output plain-text groups to stdout in the shape documented in the PRD ("Output Shape" section): `Group <N>  occurrences=<K>  score=<S>` header, `preview:` line, then numbered `file:line in Type.Member` occurrences
`score` is just the occurrence count × statement count in US-201 (stable placeholder; richer ranking lands in US-203)
Exclude groups where every occurrence contains only boilerplate (single `return`, single `throw new NotImplementedException()`, or an empty block) — document the exclusion list in FindDuplicatesCore
Info.Mutates = false, Info.JsonOutput = false (US-205 flips JsonOutput when `--json` is wired), Info.Category = "Analysis — duplication", Info.Examples has at least 2 invocations
Register in App.cs via reflection (no manual list edit); command auto-discovered

Create tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Analysis/FindDuplicatesTests.cs using AdhocProjectBuilder covering: exact duplicates inside one file detected, exact duplicates across files detected, no duplicates returns empty group list, `--min-statements=5` filters out a 3-statement duplicate, `--min-occurrences=3` filters out a 2-occurrence group, boilerplate-only blocks are not reported
Diagnostics/progress (file-count, method-count, candidate-count) written to stderr; results to stdout (FR-7)

userStories.title: find-duplicates — canonicalise identifiers, literals, and trivia
userStories.description: As a developer, I want structurally identical code with renamed locals or changed literal values to be grouped together so duplicate detection is useful beyond copy-paste clones.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a BlockNormalizer (or equivalent) under src/RoslynTools/Core that rewrites a statement-window syntax tree into a canonical form: local identifiers replaced with sequenced placeholders (`$L0`, `$L1`, …), parameter references replaced with sequenced placeholders (`$P0`, `$P1`, …), literals replaced with type-preserving placeholders (`$I0`, `$S0`, `$B0` for int/string/bool etc.), trivia stripped
Control-flow shape must be preserved verbatim — `if`/`else`/`while`/`for`/`foreach`/`switch`/`try` nodes stay in place
Type names and member-access on types are NOT canonicalised (invocation target identity matters for extractability) — document this decision in the normalizer
FindDuplicatesCore groups by the canonical-form hash instead of the verbatim hash from US-201
Each DuplicateOccurrence records the substitution map used to reach the canonical form (placeholder → original-identifier/literal) so later stories and users can inspect why a match was grouped

Add tests to FindDuplicatesTests.cs covering: renamed local variable still groups, renamed parameter still groups, changed integer literal still groups, changed string literal still groups, different control-flow (if vs while with same body) does NOT group, different invocation target (a.Foo() vs a.Bar()) does NOT group, whitespace/comment-only difference groups
Existing US-201 tests continue to pass unchanged (exact duplicates must still group under the stricter hash)
dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx succeeds
dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal all green
dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes passes
userStories.notes: Use a CSharpSyntaxRewriter driven by a per-window SymbolTable that records first-use order for stable placeholder assignment. Use SemanticModel to distinguish local/parameter/field references. Depends on US-201.

userStories.title: find-duplicates — overlap suppression and deterministic ranking
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the command to suppress redundant overlapping matches so the output highlights meaningful duplicate groups instead of hundreds of near-identical windows.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an overlap-suppression pass in FindDuplicatesCore after grouping: when two groups' occurrences overlap in the same method and one group's windows are proper sub-sequences of the other's, the smaller group is suppressed unless it also occurs in a location not covered by the larger

Ranking score replaces the US-201 placeholder: `score = log(occurrenceCount) × statementCount × extractabilityWeight` where extractabilityWeight is 1.0 in this story (US-207 refines it); document the formula in FindDuplicatesCore
Groups are emitted in descending score order; ties broken deterministically by (first-occurrence file path, first-occurrence line)
Output is stable across repeated runs on the same source (deterministic group ids: hash of canonical-form + sorted occurrence file:line set)

Add tests to FindDuplicatesTests.cs covering: overlapping windows → only the largest useful block is reported, a sub-block that also appears standalone elsewhere is kept, ranking order is stable across two runs, two identical runs produce identical group ids
Existing US-201 and US-202 tests continue to pass

dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal all green
dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes passes
userStories.notes: Suppression is the main noise source in clone-detection tools — spend tests here. Depends on US-202.

userStories.title: find-duplicates — JSON output
userStories.description: As an AI agent or tooling user, I want duplicate groups in JSON so I can rank, filter, and act on them programmatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `--json` flag to FindDuplicatesCommand

`checks[]` is an empty array in this story (US-207 populates it)
Empty results emit `{"mode":"structural","groups":[]}` with exit 0

Use SymbolFormatter helpers where applicable; do not re-roll a new JsonSerializerOptions instance

userStories.title: find-duplicates — semantic mode via pluggable IEmbeddingProvider
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an optional semantic mode that surfaces likely near-duplicate blocks even when they are not exact structural matches.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `--mode <structural|semantic>` flag to FindDuplicatesCommand; default is `structural`; `--top <N>` caps semantic-group output (default 25)

Create src/RoslynTools/Core/IEmbeddingProvider.cs with a small interface: `ValueTask<ReadOnlyMemory<float>> EmbedAsync(string text, CancellationToken ct)` plus a `string Name { get; }` and `int Dimensions { get; }`

Ship src/RoslynTools/Core/DeterministicBagOfTokensProvider.cs implementing IEmbeddingProvider — zero external dependencies, bag-of-tokens hashed into a fixed-dimension (default 256) float vector; this is the default local provider and satisfies FR-3 "works fully offline"
Provider is pluggable: the core accepts an IEmbeddingProvider via parameter; registration for real providers (e.g. ONNX-backed) is left as a future story but the interface MUST be stable

Semantic mode pipeline: reuse US-202 candidate generation + normalization → embed each normalized block via the provider → build nearest-neighbor groups by cosine similarity (threshold configurable via `--similarity <0..1>`, default 0.85) → re-rank by applying the same deterministic structural checks used in structural mode and attach the pass/fail results to each group's `checks[]`
Semantic results are clearly labelled: plain-text output prefixes semantic group headers with `[semantic]` and includes the similarity score; JSON groups have `mode: "semantic"`
Semantic results are NEVER marked `extractability: extractable` in v1 — force `likely_extractable` or `discovery_only` regardless of checks (FR-9, Principle "Safe handoff")
If an embedding provider throws or is not configured, the command falls back to structural mode with a WARN on stderr and exit code 0 (graceful degradation per FR-8)

Add tests to FindDuplicatesTests.cs covering: semantic mode with the deterministic stub provider surfaces a near-duplicate pair that structural mode missed, similarity threshold filters out low-similarity pairs, provider-throws fallback to structural with WARN, semantic group never has `extractability: extractable`, `--top 5` caps output
Existing structural-mode tests continue to pass (default mode unchanged)
README.md documents the pluggable provider interface with a one-paragraph "writing your own provider" example

userStories.title: find-duplicates — extraction-readiness diagnostics
userStories.description: As a developer, I want each duplicate group to indicate whether it looks safely extractable so I can focus on actionable results first.
acceptanceCriteria: Add ExtractabilityAnalyzer under src/RoslynTools/Core that, given a canonical block + its occurrences, emits a list of Check records: `{ name, status, detail }` where status ∈ { pass, warn, fail }

Checks implemented in v1: `parameterizable-inputs` (placeholders map to identifiers reachable at each occurrence; fails if one site has a literal where another has an expression), `single-output` (block produces ≤1 outward value per data-flow analysis), `no-control-flow-escape` (no `return`/`yield`/`goto`/labelled `break` that would not round-trip through an extracted method), `no-ref-out-params` (no ref/out parameter usage), `consistent-captured-state` (captured fields/props the same at every occurrence)
DuplicateGroup.extractability is derived: all checks pass → `extractable`; at least one warn, no fails → `likely_extractable`; any fail OR semantic-mode group → `discovery_only`
Checks[] populated in both plain-text (one line each under the group header) and JSON output
Ranking score (from US-203) multiplies by extractabilityWeight: extractable=1.0, likely_extractable=0.7, discovery_only=0.3

Add tests to FindDuplicatesTests.cs covering: a fully extractable group is labelled `extractable`, a group with a literal-where-identifier-needed is labelled `discovery_only` with `parameterizable-inputs: fail`, a group with a `return` inside the block is `discovery_only` with `no-control-flow-escape: fail`, a group with differing captured fields is `likely_extractable` with `consistent-captured-state: warn`, semantic-mode groups cannot be `extractable`
Existing structural and semantic tests continue to pass
README.md documents the check list and extractability levels
